title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative:
1. Over the period 2022-2023, Zimbabwe through the support of the African Development Bank (AfDB) has operationalised the Anchor Enterprise Business Model to promote inclusive entrepreneurship and SME development in the horticulture, light manufacturing, agro-processing and small-scale mining value chains in urban and rural areas to promote entrepreneurship, business resilience and SME development in a currently volatile and insecure enterprise environment in Zimbabwe: a. One (1) anchor enterprise - Tasimudzwa Women Milling (Pvt) Ltd in Guruve District was established to primarily value-add gold ore. The enterprise is co-owned and integrates 125 women artisanal miners into the small-scale mining value chain through running the gold milling centre which is servicing at least 3380 (980 female and 2400 male) artisanal miners from the district and surrounding areas. There has been a strong focus on ensuring an inclusive business model for especially women entrepreneurs. i. The plant integrates modern mining techniques which include mercury-free gold-processing which is safe for the miners and environmentally friendly. b. One (1) Safe Market Place – Chesvingo Safe Market Place in Masvingo town has been constructed to provide inclusive safe working spaces for women traders and to facilitate delivery of integrated services for survivors of Gender-Based-Violence (GBV). The Safe Market place is managed by Masvingo City Council with support from national and local government. This is a good example of an innovative business model and hub in which GBV has been addressed though the safe marketplace thereby allowing women traders in a safe and secure environment. 2.The Government of Zimbabwe through the Ministries of Women Affairs, Community, Small and Medium Enterprise Development and Youth, Sport, Arts and Recreation has rolled-out the Sustainable and Resilient Enterprises (SURE) training programme in six(6) districts. 1. With support from the AfDB and the Government of Zimbabwe, the ILO provided technical assistance as well as financial assistance through the Sustainable Enterprise Development for Women and Youth (SEDWAY) programme towards: a. Establishment of the gold milling anchor enterprise, including the procurement and installation of the plant and equipment. The Anchor Enterprise received additional working capital and business development services to start-up operations valued at $700,000. The 125 women artisanal miners were trained on mine safety and health, modern mining techniques and principles of corporate governance.
b. The ILO invested $70,000 in infrastructure, in addition to investments by the Ministry of Women Affairs, Community, Small and Enterprise Development and the Masvingo City Council to establish a Safe Market Place in Masvingo. At least 90 women traders are benefiting from the workspace and the greater community as access to a victim friendly police post and counselling services for GBV survivors.
2. In 2023, With support from the AfDB and the Government of Zimbabwe, the ILO provided technical assistance through the Business Growth for Young Entrepreneurs (BG4YE) Project and ran a Training of Trainers’ Certification course on the ILO Sustainable and Resilient Enterprises (SURE) Programme for 17 Business Development DS providers from 6 districts (Mutoko, Bulawayo, Masvingo, Umguza, Karoi and Masvingo). The 17 BDS providers trained 340 growth-oriented enterprises as part of their certification process.
